what do seniors need to do before gradua.question: What do seniors need to do before graduation?

variants.answer:
Here’s a summary of what Vista Ridge High School seniors (Class of 2027) need to do before graduation, based on the information for this school year:

- **Order Cap & Gown:**  
  All seniors are required to order the Cap, Gown & Tassel Unit from Herff Jones. You’ll receive order packets and details at the senior meeting. Only the cap, gown, and tassel are required; other items are optional.

- **Fill Out FAFSA:**  
  Completing the [FAFSA](https://studentaid.gov/) is a graduation requirement. The application opens October 1, and the priority deadline for most Texas universities is January 15.

- **Meet College Application Deadlines:**  
  Many Texas universities have an Early Action/Priority Deadline of October 15. Check with each university for their specific dates.

- **Senior Panoramic Photo:**  
  Attend the senior panoramic picture on Wednesday, March 24th during Ranger Time.

- **Awards and Activities:**  
  - Prom (details to come)
  - Senior Scramble (details to come)
  - Senior Awards (invitation only)
  - Senior SAIL – a celebration and hangout for seniors

- **Elementary Graduation Walks:**  
  You may participate in the LISD tradition of walking at your former elementary school in your cap and gown. Find more details [here](https://news.leanderisd.org/class-of-2026-senior-walks-schedule-announced/).

- **Graduation Practice & Clap Out:**  
  Attend graduation practice and the traditional clap out immediately afterwards.

- **Clear Obligations:**  
  All school obligations and required hours must be cleared to pick up your cap and gown and participate in graduation.

- **Graduation Ceremony:**  
  Graduation is scheduled for Saturday, May 29th at 10am at the Cedar Park Center. More info is available on the [District Graduation page](https://www.leanderisd.org/graduation/).

- **Cap Decorating:**  
  Follow the cap decorating guidelines—keep it appropriate and avoid prohibited content.

- **Transition Your School Google Account:**  
  After graduation (usually around July), your school Google account will be moved to an alum account (@alum.leanderisd.org) and will be active for one year. Download any important files you wish to keep.

- **Other Traditions:**  
  Participate in Baccalaureate and Project Graduation ([Project Graduation info here](https://sites.google.com/view/vistaridgeprojectgrad/home)).

If you have specific questions about steps or need personal guidance, your counselor is your best resource. If you’re looking for more details on any of these events or requirements, the [Seniors 2027 page](https://vrhs.leanderisd.org/seniors-2027#h.8303diwz6ah) is a good starting point.

Let me know if you need information on any part of the process, or if you need help connecting with a counselor or office. Good luck, and enjoy your senior year as a Vista Ridge Ranger!

- Submit an absence note or medical documentation by email from the parent/guardian's email address (the one on file) to **VRHSattendance@leanderisd.org**.
- You can also hand deliver a note to the Attendance Office.

what clubs and organizations are offered.question: What clubs and organizations are offered?

variants.answer:
Vista Ridge High School offers a variety of clubs and organizations that give students opportunities to explore interests, develop leadership skills, serve the community, and prepare for careers. Here are some of the clubs and their purposes, as listed in the school's resources:

- **National Technical Honor Society**  
  Focuses on career-focused workshops (resume writing, mock interviews), leadership programs, community service projects, and recognition events. Open to anyone enrolled in a CTE program.  
  Sponsor: Miguel Valenzuela

- **Students in Medicine**  
  Provides mini lessons on medical topics and hands-on labs on campus, such as learning about vaccines and performing lab techniques like electrophoresis.  
  Sponsor: Jacob Hoffman

- **STEM Competition Club**  
  Offers preparation and tutoring for STEM competitions like USAPhO, USACO, USABO, along with volunteering to promote STEM in elementary and middle schools.  
  Sponsor: Vanessa Ramirez

- **Key Club**  
  Engages students in community service, character building, and leadership through hands-on projects and a focus on compassion and inclusivity.  
  Sponsor: Caitlyn Goodfellow

- **Health Occupations Students of America (HOSA)**  
  Focuses on medical career information, competitions, volunteer opportunities, and experiences like job shadowing and mini med schools. Open to students enrolled in Biomed CTE courses.  
  Sponsors: Jesse Leake and Cori Crandus

For the full list and details of all clubs and organizations, you can visit the [Clubs & Organizations](https://vrhs.leanderisd.org/campus_information/clubs) page on the Vista Ridge High School website.

If you have a specific interest, let me know and I can help point you to the right club!
